derivationStages.stageRecord: This analysis gives each alternative its own external-argument and inflectional domain. The first clause has overt 你; the second has an independently merged silent pronominal subject. The workspace therefore contains two external-argument heads and two T heads, together with one alternative coordinator and one interrogative C. The silent pronoun is not a movement copy or a deleted occurrence of 你. Its interpretation will be linked to the overt subject when the argument structures are built. As in the predicate-coordination analysis, 喝茶 is syntactically decomposed into a verb and nominal complement.
derivationStages.statement: Select the lexical objects for clausal coordination with a null second subject.

values.operation: associate the syntactic verb and its nominal complement with one supplied token

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the first 喝 with 茶, establishing 茶 as its theme. Independently merge the second 喝 with 咖啡, establishing 咖啡 as its theme. Each complex object inherits its verb's label. Then associate the first verb and its nominal complement jointly with the supplied token 喝茶. The association records the supplied orthographic boundary without collapsing the two syntax objects or introducing incorporation.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the two verb–object predicates.

values.interpretation: coreference with the addressee denoted by 你
values.syntacticStatus: independently merged pronoun, not a copy of the overt subject

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the first external-argument head with the tea predicate and then merge 你 at its edge, establishing 你 as the agent of tea drinking. Build the coffee domain separately by merging the second external-argument head with the coffee predicate and then merging the silent pronoun at its edge, establishing that pronoun as the agent of coffee drinking. Finally, resolve the silent pronoun to the individual denoted by 你 in this parallel alternative question. This is interpretive coreference between distinct syntactic objects, not a shared movement lineage. The structure consequently contains two thematic subject positions even though only one subject is pronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Build two independent external-argument domains.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the first silent T with the tea external-argument domain and internally merge 你 at its edge. The higher occurrence pronounces 你, and its already established thematic occurrence becomes silent. Independently merge the second silent T with the coffee external-argument domain and internally merge the silent pronoun at its edge. Both occurrences of that pronoun remain silent. These operations satisfy the subject-edge requirement adopted for each T; they do not posit overt tense or agreement morphology. The two chains remain distinct, despite the coreference established between their subjects.
derivationStages.statement: Construct separate T projections and subject chains.

alternativeOrder: the coreferential null subject drinks coffee
values.interpretation: alternative propositions with separate subject and inflectional domains

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge 还是 with the coffee T projection, and then merge the tea T projection at the left edge of the resulting coordinator projection. The coordinator labels both binary combinations. It now relates complete inflectional clauses rather than subjectless verbal predicates. Its alternatives are that the addressee drinks tea and that the coreferential null subject drinks coffee. The overt order does not distinguish this higher coordination from lower predicate coordination because the second clause's subject is silent.
derivationStages.statement: Coordinate the two inflectional clauses.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the silent interrogative C with the coordinated T projections. C scopes over the alternatives introduced by 还是 and requests a choice between the two propositions. A single interrogative head supplies question force to the whole coordination; neither conjunct requires its own pronounced interrogative marker. This completed analysis differs structurally from shared-subject predicate coordination by containing two external-argument domains, two T projections, and a silent pronominal subject in the second conjunct. The sole pronounced subject is the higher copy of 你 in the first conjunct. Together with the retained joint realization of 喝茶, the pronounced yield exactly matches all five supplied tokens.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the clausal-coordination alternative question.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The Swedish input is analyzed as a declarative clause with a negative pronominal subject and an indefinite pronominal object. Ingen and någonting each project a DP headed by a pronominal D; neither requires an unpronounced lexical noun. Within the VP-internal subject analysis adopted here, Ingen occupies Spec-VP, while någonting is the complement of såg. The verb assigns the subject the Experiencer role and the object the Theme role. As a transitive verb, it also governs its object and assigns structural accusative Case. IP contains this VP and a silent finite past-tense I; declarative C is initially a separate head. Såg is introduced in its attested, lexically inflected form, not assembled from separately pronounced tense material. Its subsequent head movement will establish its relation to I. The negative subject and the indefinite object are not two negative expressions: någonting is available here as an existential indefinite under negative scope.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the argument structure, lexical Case, and initial clausal workspace.

relations.relation: V-to-I head movement and tense matching
Preservation of object Case through the verbal chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: First, såg moves from V to the previously introduced I, forming a complex finite head and leaving a silent V-trace. This local head movement relates the lexically past-tense verb to finite past I without positing a separate overt tense exponent. The V-chain preserves the object's accusative licensing through the governed verbal trace. Ingen then raises from Spec-VP to Spec-IP, leaving a DP-trace in its theta position. This A-movement gives the subject access to nominative Case from finite I; it does not assign another theta role. Both movements start from positions present in the preceding workspace. The derivation uses traces rather than unpronounced lexical copies.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the verb to I and the subject to Spec-IP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Declarative C takes the existing IP as its complement. The complex finite I head then raises to C, leaving an I-trace in its immediately preceding position. The result is successive-cyclic V-to-I-to-C movement, not a direct jump from V to C. This is the head-movement component of Swedish main-clause verb-second syntax. Spec-CP is not yet filled, so this intermediate workspace does not yet represent the completed surface order. The subject remains in Spec-IP, and its nominative and theta dependencies are preserved.
derivationStages.statement: Build the declarative CP and move the finite head to C.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Ingen moves from the already established Spec-IP to Spec-CP, leaving a subject trace in Spec-IP. This is A-bar movement into the Swedish declarative prefield; it need not imply a contrastive discourse topic. The resulting subject chain retains its nominative position in Spec-IP and its theta position in Spec-VP. With one constituent in Spec-CP and the finite verb in C, the pronounced order is exactly Ingen såg någonting. The negative quantificational subject c-commands the object, licensing the polarity-sensitive existential use of någonting. Its interpretation is that no person saw anything, not negative concord between two negative DPs. No additional scope movement is required for this reading. The subject's quantificational dependency binds its silent subject positions, and the head-movement chains connect the finite verb to its lower traces; there are no overt anaphors requiring a separate binding analysis.
derivationStages.statement: Complete subject-initial V2 order and establish negative scope over the object indefinite.

cases.sentence: Ich weiß, dass er das Buch hat lesen wollen.

values.construction: Coherent modal complementation without an intervening IP or PRO
Ersatzinfinitiv under perfect haben with a dependent infinitive

values.restriction: Overt dass occupies C; the embedded finite verb does not raise to C

derivationStages.stageRecord: The embedded clause is initially assembled with head-final VP and IP projections and the overt complementizer dass. The analysis uses DP structure for nominal expressions and the classical GB option of generating the external argument in Spec-IP. Lesen assigns Theme to das Buch and its external Agent role to er through the verbal projection. Wollen takes the infinitival lesen projection as a coherent modal complement: there is no separate infinitival IP or PRO subject. Hat selects the modal projection and introduces perfect aspect. This combination licenses the Ersatzinfinitiv wollen instead of the ordinary participle gewollt; lesen remains the infinitive selected by the modal. Lesen governs and assigns accusative to das Buch, while finite I licenses nominative on er. The lexical finite form hat agrees with er; its association with I will be established by head movement. Dass selects the finite IP and occupies C, excluding embedded verb-second movement into that position. The terminal order here is an underlying order, not yet the input order.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the head-final embedded clause and its coherent perfect–modal construction.

values.chain: The raised lexical verb binds its head trace and retains its argument and Case dependencies

derivationStages.stageRecord: Lesen moves from the lexical head position displayed in the preceding workspace and left-adjoins to wollen, creating the complex head lesen wollen. A silent head trace remains in the lexical VP. This is local head movement to the immediately selecting verbal head; it does not move das Buch or introduce another subject. The raised lexical head binds its trace, and its original theta and Case relations are preserved through the chain. This intermediate cluster must be present before it can move to the perfect auxiliary.
derivationStages.statement: Raise lesen to the modal and form the lower verbal cluster.

values.construction: Auxiliary-first Oberfeld order in the Ersatzinfinitiv construction
values.locality: Movement targets the immediately selecting verbal head
values.operation: Right-adjunction of the infinitival verbal cluster to the perfect auxiliary

derivationStages.stageRecord: The already formed lesen wollen head moves from the modal head position to the immediately higher perfect auxiliary. This analysis adopts the verb-raising treatment of German auxiliary inversion: in the Ersatzinfinitiv construction, the lower verbal cluster right-adjoins to haben, yielding hat lesen wollen rather than lesen wollen hat. A silent complex-head trace remains in the modal position and is bound by the raised cluster. Right-adjunction is a construction-specific linearization commitment, not movement of hat to embedded C. The result is still a head-final perfect VP externally, even though its complex head begins with the auxiliary.
derivationStages.statement: Derive auxiliary-first order inside the three-verb cluster.

values.licensing: Association of finite hat with embedded inflection
values.operation: V-to-I movement of the entire verbal cluster

values.requirement: Finite verb in C and one constituent in Spec-CP

derivationStages.stageRecord: First, the perfect verbal cluster moves from the auxiliary head position to the immediately higher, clause-final I, leaving a head trace. The finite auxiliary thereby associates with the embedded finite inflection; the cluster's internal order is unchanged, and dass remains in C. Next, the completed embedded CP is merged as the propositional complement of matrix weiß in a head-final VP. Ich is generated in matrix Spec-IP and receives the Knower role, while the CP receives the propositional Content role. Matrix finite I licenses nominative on Ich and carries first-person singular present features matching weiß. An initially empty matrix C provides the target for subsequent verb-second movement. No extraposition of the complement CP is required: movement of the matrix verb will leave this complement following the pronounced verb.
derivationStages.statement: Complete embedded V-to-I movement and establish the matrix clause.

values.licensing: Association of weiß with matrix finite inflection

derivationStages.stageRecord: Weiß moves from the matrix V position shown previously and adjoins to matrix I, leaving a silent lexical head trace. This establishes the finite verbal head that can subsequently move to C. The step is recorded separately because I-to-C movement must start from an already established I position; direct movement from V to C would skip the intervening head. The verb's selection of the embedded CP and its theta relation to Ich remain connected to the original predicate position through the head chain.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the matrix verb to finite I.

values.chainLicensing: The raised DP binds its trace and retains the theta role and nominative Case of its subject position
values.function: Occupation of the matrix preverbal field

values.condition: Each overt pronoun is free in its local governing domain

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix finite I head moves to the empty matrix C, leaving an I trace and completing the successive V-to-I-to-C head chain. Ich then moves from the previously displayed Spec-IP position to Spec-CP, leaving a DP trace. This A-bar movement supplies the single preverbal constituent without assigning a new theta role or Case: the subject chain retains the Knower role and nominative licensed at its IP position. The head and subject chains are local and their traces are bound by the raised occurrences. The pronouns Ich and er have no coindexed local antecedents, satisfying Principle B; the modal construction has no additional silent pronominal subject. The final pronounced order is Ich weiß dass er das Buch hat lesen wollen. The embedded auxiliary-first sequence is internal to its raised verbal cluster, whereas the matrix finite verb occupies C. These are different structural dependencies, and neither requires extraposition of the embedded CP.
derivationStages.statement: Complete matrix verb-second order and the analysis of the input.

cases.sentence: The man whose car was stolen called the police.

values.interpretation: The relative variable denotes the possessor of the car.

values.externalArgument: suppressed; no overt or silent agent DP projected

derivationStages.stageRecord: Use a DP-based X-bar analysis within Government and Binding Theory. The relative possessive determiner whose heads the DP whose car; its genitive interpretation is internal to that DP, with car as the possessum. Whose is treated as a lexical relative D, without an additional possessor-movement derivation. First establish this possessive dependency. Next, stolen selects the car DP as its complement and assigns it the Theme theta-role. Passive morphology suppresses an overt external argument and prevents the passive verb from assigning structural accusative Case; no silent agent DP is posited. Finally, finite I, realized as was, selects the passive VP. Stolen is introduced as an already inflected passive participle, so this analysis does not require participial head movement. The subject position is not yet filled, and the theme DP has not yet received structural Case.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the relative clause's passive predicate and its underlying theme argument.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move the previously represented DP whose car from the complement of stolen to Spec-IP, leaving an unpronounced DP trace in the complement position. This A-movement fills the finite clause's subject position without assigning a second theta-role. The resulting A-chain connects the raised DP to the Theme position selected by stolen. Finite was then licenses nominative Case on the subject occurrence and hence on its chain; singular agreement follows the head noun car, not the possessor denoted by whose. This intermediate subject position is represented explicitly because it is the source of the subsequent relative movement.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the passive theme to the relative clause's subject position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Introduce a silent relative C above the existing IP. Move the entire DP whose car from the explicitly represented Spec-IP position to Spec-CP, leaving a subject trace. The relative feature of whose licenses pied-piping of its containing DP: whose does not move independently out of the nominal. The movement is local to this clause and involves no subject–auxiliary inversion; was remains in I. The relative C licenses the fronted operator-containing DP. The resulting dependency contains an A-bar link from Spec-CP to the subject position and the previously established A-link from the subject position to the passive complement. Nominative Case is associated with the intermediate subject position, while the Theme role remains associated with the lowest position. The operator's external nominal antecedent has not yet been attached.
derivationStages.statement: Form the relative CP by pied-piping whose car into Spec-CP.

values.distinction: The antecedent is the man; the moved Theme DP denotes his car.

values.scope: man together with the restrictive relative clause

derivationStages.stageRecord: Project man as the nominal head and adjoin the completed relative CP to N', forming the restriction man whose car was stolen. The exact input supplies an integrated relative clause, rather than a comma-delimited supplementary relative. Establish the CP's restrictive modification of the nominal first. Then identify the relative possessor variable expressed by whose with the man described by the head nominal. This antecedent dependency concerns the possessor, not the entire moved DP whose car: the man is not the Theme of stolen. Finally, The takes the modified NP as its complement, placing both the nominal description and the restrictive relative within the definite DP. The relative clause is an adjunct of the nominal, not a complement selected by man.
derivationStages.statement: Attach the restrictive relative clause inside the matrix subject DP.

relations.relation: matrix object selection and theta assignment

values.licensingConfiguration: active V governing its DP complement

values.morphologicalCommitment: Called is an inflected lexical V; silent I encodes finite features without a separately realized affix.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Build the DP the police and merge it as the complement of called. The active verb selects this DP, assigns it the role of the contacted party, and governs it for structural accusative Case. Combine that predicate with the previously constructed subject DP in Spec-IP. In the traditional GB subject architecture adopted here, the matrix subject is base-generated in Spec-IP, rather than raised from a VP-internal position; the verbal predicate assigns it the external Agent role through predication. Finite matrix I licenses nominative Case on this subject. Called is introduced as the inflected past-tense lexical verb, while silent I represents its finite tense and agreement features, not a separately pronounced tense affix; no additional morphological movement is asserted. Finally, a silent declarative C heads the root CP. The completed structure distinguishes the active matrix clause from the embedded passive relative: the man is the caller, his car is the stolen Theme, and the police are the contacted party. All supplied tokens are realized once, with the two relative-clause traces and both complementizers unpronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the active matrix clause and the sentence's GB analysis.

cases.sentence: Jean a fait réparer la voiture.

values.configuration: The transitive infinitive governs its NP complement.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The analysis uses classical NP, VP, IP, and CP projections. Within the object NP, la occupies the determiner position and voiture heads N′. Réparer heads V′ and takes this NP as its complement. Réparer assigns the Theme role to la voiture and governs it for accusative Case: an infinitive lacks finite nominative licensing, but a transitive infinitive can still license its object. The workspace is not yet a complete clause. In particular, the external argument of réparer awaits licensing by the causative construction introduced next. The lexical form réparer is already infinitival; no independent embedded tense projection has been built.
derivationStages.statement: Build the infinitival predicate and its direct object.

values.complementType: infinitival VP without independent Tense or a syntactic subject

values.licensing: Implicit causee licensed by the causative construction; no additional NP or PRO is projected.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Participial fait is introduced as the causative verb faire, selecting the previously built infinitival VP. This is a coherent faire-infinitive construction, not an independently tensed complement or an ordinary subject-control infinitive. The selected VP has no separate IP, nominative subject position, or PRO subject. In this VP-complement implementation of the French causative, argument composition licenses the repairer's external role as an implicit causee rather than projecting an additional silent NP. Thus the sentence leaves the identity of the repairer unspecified; it does not syntactically identify that participant with Jean. Jean is introduced in the specifier of the matrix VP under the VP-internal subject hypothesis and receives the Causer role from the causative predicate. The thematic and accusative relations between réparer and la voiture remain unchanged. Neither infinitival head movement nor a covert causee movement is posited.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the causative VP and its argument structure.

values.compoundTense: passé composé of the causative predicate

values.subjectRequirement: Specifier of IP must be filled.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Finite avoir, pronounced a, is introduced directly in I, and its I′ takes the causative VP as complement. This implementation therefore does not require an auxiliary movement from an unrecorded lower position. The auxiliary selects the participial form fait, producing the passé composé of the causative predicate; réparer remains the infinitive selected by faire. The supplied whole-word forms express their inflection without separate morphological realization groups. Finite I carries present-tense and third-person singular features and supplies the nominative licensing needed by the matrix subject. Jean is still in its previously established VP-internal theta position, however, so subject raising and nominative assignment have not yet occurred. Specifier of IP remains unfilled in this intermediate workspace.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce finite auxiliary structure above the causative VP.

values.chainThetaRole: Causer, assigned at the base position
values.emptyCategoryLicensing: The raised NP antecedent-governs its trace.
values.movement: specifier of VP to specifier of IP

values.condition: Each referential NP is free; neither has a coindexed c-commanding A-binder.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Jean raises from the VP-internal position shown in the preceding workspace to specifier of IP, leaving an unpronounced NP trace. This is A-movement: it fills the finite subject position without assigning another theta-role. The raised NP and its trace form one argument chain, receiving the Causer role at its lower position. The raised NP c-commands and antecedent-governs the trace across the selected matrix VP, satisfying the trace's Empty Category Principle requirement. In the resulting specifier–head configuration, finite I licenses nominative on Jean and agrees with its third-person singular features. Finally, a phonologically null declarative C takes the completed IP as complement; there is no interrogative inversion or movement to C. Jean and la voiture are referential NPs with no coindexed A-binder, satisfying Binding Principle C. The completed pronounced sequence is exactly Jean a fait réparer la voiture. The absent overt causee does not create a separate subject-control reading: the repairer's unspecified identity belongs to the same causative structure.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the subject chain and the declarative clause.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Project loves as V, taking someone as its NP complement, and place Everyone in Spec-IP as the external argument. This uses the traditional GB base-generated subject analysis rather than a VP-internal subject derivation. Both indefinite pronouns are complete NPs with nominal heads. First, loves assigns its external experiencer role to Everyone and its internal theme role to someone. Next, finite I licenses nominative Case on the subject, and V governs and assigns accusative Case to its complement. Finally, establish the agreement and tense dependency between the subject, finite I, and loves. Adopt a lexicalist treatment of English inflection: loves enters as an inflected verb licensed by this dependency, so neither overt V-to-I movement nor a separate affix-lowering derivation is posited. The silent I head expresses present tense and third-person singular agreement. This overt structure is shared by both scope readings; scope will be established by covert quantifier raising.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the overt clause and its argument structure.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Covertly raise someone from the previously established complement position and adjoin its NP to IP. Represent GB quantifier raising with an occurrence-based copy notation: the new higher occurrence is silent at PF and interpreted as the existential operator at LF; the lower occurrence retains its pronunciation but is interpreted as the operator's variable. This is the copy equivalent of the usual GB operator–trace representation, not an additional overt NP. The higher NP c-commands and A′-binds its lower occurrence. The chain retains the theme role and accusative Case licensed at the complement position; adjunction assigns neither a new theta role nor new Case. The clause-internal dependency crosses no island. This intermediate workspace establishes the existential adjunction site before the universal is raised above it.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the existential quantifier to the first LF adjunction position.

values.reading: For every person, there is a possibly different person whom that person loves.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Raise Everyone from the subject position shown in the preceding workspace and adjoin its silent operator occurrence to the already expanded IP. Its pronounced lower occurrence becomes the LF subject variable. The universal operator c-commands and A′-binds that occurrence, while the subject chain retains its external theta role and nominative Case. This is another clause-internal QR dependency, without an island crossing. Next, establish scope from the completed LF hierarchy: the universal operator asymmetrically c-commands the existential operator, yielding ∀x[person(x) → ∃y[person(y) ∧ love(x,y)]]. Thus each person loves at least one person, with no requirement that the loved person be the same for everyone. Operator binding here is the A′-binding of QR variables, not an anaphoric dependency governed by Principle A. The lower copies remain pronounced in the original order, accounting for Everyone loves someone while the silent higher copies supply LF scope.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the universal-wide-scope reading.

values.realization: lexically inflected V remains in situ

derivationStages.stageRecord: Project loves as V with someone as its NP complement and Everyone in Spec-IP. Adopt traditional GB subject base-generation, with no VP-internal subject movement, and analyze both indefinite pronouns as nominally headed NPs. First, loves assigns Everyone the external experiencer role and someone the internal theme role. Next, finite I licenses nominative Case on Everyone, and V governs and assigns accusative Case to someone. Finally, establish present-tense and third-person singular agreement licensing between the subject, silent finite I, and the lexically inflected verb loves. On this lexicalist treatment, the verb remains in V; neither V-to-I movement nor affix lowering is part of the derivation. The overt clause does not itself decide the relative scope of the two quantifiers. The following LF operations derive the existential-wide-scope reading.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the overt clause and its argument structure.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Covertly raise Everyone from the previously established Spec-IP position and adjoin its NP to IP. Use an occurrence-based copy representation of GB QR: the higher occurrence is silent at PF and interpreted as a universal operator, while the lower occurrence remains pronounced and is interpreted as its variable. This represents the same LF dependency as the traditional operator–trace notation rather than adding another pronounced subject. The higher occurrence c-commands and A′-binds the lower occurrence. The chain retains the experiencer role and nominative Case of the subject position; the adjoined position supplies no additional theta role or Case. This clause-internal operation crosses no island. Establishing this intermediate structure allows the existential operator to be adjoined outside the universal's scope position in the next stage.

values.reading: There is at least one person whom everyone loves.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Raise someone from the complement position present in the preceding workspace and adjoin its silent operator occurrence outside the IP already containing the raised universal. Its lower, pronounced occurrence is interpreted as the object variable. The existential operator c-commands and A′-binds that occurrence; its chain retains the theme role and accusative Case licensed in the complement position. This clause-internal QR dependency crosses no island. Next, establish the scope relation from the completed hierarchy: the existential operator asymmetrically c-commands the universal operator, yielding ∃y[person(y) ∧ ∀x[person(x) → love(x,y)]]. There is therefore at least one person whom everyone loves. This does not assert that there is only one such person. The binding dependencies are A′ operator–variable dependencies, not Principle A anaphoric dependencies. Both higher copies are silent, and both lower copies remain pronounced, preserving exactly the overt order Everyone loves someone despite the inverse LF scope.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the existential-wide-scope reading.

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines compró with the interrogative pronominal D Qué. The resulting object is labeled VP by the selecting verb; Qué is the internal argument, interpreted as the thing purchased. Juan is selected as a proper-name D, alongside an unpronounced transitive v, past-tense T, and interrogative C. Projection labels abbreviate labels determined by the participating heads, not independently supplied phrase-structure templates. Compró is retained as one inflected lexical terminal: this analysis does not segment its written form into separate morphemes.

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge first combines transitive v with VP and then merges Juan as the external argument. Juan receives the agent role, distinguishing this nominal from the interrogative object. Transitive v licenses structural accusative on Qué. Juan remains in its thematic position; this analysis will not require subject raising to the edge of TP.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce Juan as the external argument of transitive v.

This local step supplies the verbal complex that can subsequently raise to T without skipping v.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge copies Qué from the complement of V to an outer edge of vP, above the external argument. derivationStages.stageRecord: T externally merges with the phase-edge structure. Its person-number probe agrees with Juan and licenses nominative Case; the intervening accusative wh object is inactive for this nominative dependency. T has no obligatory nominal edge requirement in this analysis, so Juan stays in its external-argument position. The verbal complex then raises from v to T, with the entire lower complex becoming silent. Finally, the higher V occurrence is licensed as the already inflected past, third-person singular form compró by T and its agreement dependency. T itself has no separate exponent. Verb raising above the unmoved subject establishes the verb-before-subject order without movement of the verb to C.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Interrogative C externally merges with TP and establishes the clause's question force. Its interrogative edge requirement then attracts Qué from the previously established vP edge to the CP edge. The CP occurrence is pronounced and the intermediate occurrence becomes silent; the original complement occurrence remains silent. C takes scope over the proposition and binds the object variable through this movement chain, yielding a question about what Juan purchased. C remains unpronounced and does not attract T in this derivation. The completed structure consequently pronounces Qué, compró, Juan in that order. Juan is the thematic subject, not a vocative or an object.
